title: Python SDK: ChatFlow event adapter + Fallback Conductor for graceful streaming degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Users of the Python SDK need a higher-level, ergonomic surface for handling streaming chat completions so they can attach callbacks for partial output, manage cancellations/backpressure, and provide automated fallbacks when streaming fails (e.g., network blips, model overload). Current lower-level event iterator patterns are flexible but verbose; teams repeatedly reimplement similar glue logic (checkpointing, merge heuristics, safe sync/async hooks) across apps.

Goal: Build a composable ChatFlowEventAdapter and a Fallback Conductor in the Python SDK that: (1) exposes a simple context-managed streaming API with sync/async callback hooks, (2) provides safe cancellation and backpressure tokens, (3) automatically falls back to a non-streaming completion or cheaper model variant on transient failures according to policy, and (4) emits structured telemetry for partials/retries/fallbacks. The intent is to reduce copy-paste boilerplate and encourage correct retry/fallback behavior by default.
proposed_api:
Option A (recommended):

from redwood import ChatClient, ChatFlow

async with ChatFlow(client) as flow:
    # register sync or async handlers
    flow.on_partial(handle_partial)
    flow.on_final(handle_final)
    flow.on_error(handle_error)

    # start streaming; flow returns a small controller object
    controller = await flow.start_stream(prompt, model="rwd-3.7-stream")

    # controller exposes cancellation and a backpressure token
    await controller.wait_done()

---
Key semantics:
- on_partial receives (chunk_text, meta) and must not block the event loop; async handlers allowed
- cancel() triggers graceful drain unless force_cancel=True
- Fallback Conductor middleware can be attached via flow.with_fallback(policy=...) and initiates a one-shot non-stream completion if streaming fails repeatedly

Alternative (lower-level): EventAdapter wrapping raw HTTP SSE/GPT-streaming responses into typed events (PARTIAL, DELTA, FINAL, SIGNAL) and providing an async iterator. This remains available for advanced users.
acceptance_criteria: A. SDK exposes ChatFlow context manager with on_partial/on_final/on_error hooks working in sync and async callables
B. Controller provides cancel() and pause_backpressure() semantics; docs include pattern for cooperative backpressure from consumer code
C. Fallback Conductor triggers non-stream call according to policy (exponential backoff + max_retries) and returns consistent final payload shape
D. Telemetry emitted for every streaming session: partial_count, bytes_streamed, fallback_reason, retry_count, latency_ms
E. End-to-end unit and integration tests covering network hiccups, handler exceptions, cancel during fallback, and metrics emission
F. Developer docs and 2 small examples: chatflow_async_example.py and chatflow_sync_handler_snippet.md
technical_notes: We will build ChatFlow as a thin orchestration layer on top of the existing stream iterator code; keep low allocation path for hot paths (no per-chunk allocation when handler is noop).
Fallback Conductor performs an automatic model-variant lookup using the runtime routing hints; it should be pluggable (customer can override policy to prefer cheaper or smaller context variants).

Backpressure: implement a bounded asyncio.Queue between network reader and handlers; expose an async pause/resume API that consumers can call to reduce memory pressure. Default queue size 16 chunks, configurable via ChatFlow(queue_size=16).

Cancellation: support cooperative cancel token that signals the network reader to stop reading new frames but still allows in-flight handler tasks to complete within a timeout (configurable default 3s).
Error handling: handler exceptions must be captured and surfaced to on_error; a flag (suppress_handler_exceptions) allows failures to be logged vs bubble up to user code depending on config.

Telemetry: use existing SDK metrics pipeline; add new metric names: sdk.chatflow.partials, sdk.chatflow.fallbacks, sdk.chatflow.backpressure_pauses. Add tracing spans at start/finish and when fallback triggered.
Compatibility: maintain backward compatibility with existing stream iterator APIs; this API is additive and optional.
Security: ensure no sensitive payloads are emitted to logs by default; telemetry should redact prompt text and only emit token counts/byte sizes.
Performance: microbenchmarks should show <5% overhead vs raw iterator in the noop-handler case; benchmark targets included in PR template.
